key_insight: Real-time ontology grounding via MCP markedly improved HPO extraction by boosting precision and F1 while sharply reducing mapping errors across multiple LLMs.
clinical_relevance: For clinical genetics workflows, tool-augmented LLMs may better support phenotype capture from notes, improving downstream variant prioritization and diagnostic review.
method: Five LLMs were tested on four synthetic clinical genetics notes.
Each model ran in baseline mode and in a tool-augmented mode with real-time HPO retrieval via MCP or equivalent tool-calling.
Outputs were manually adjudicated and scored for precision, recall, F1, mapping errors, and hallucinations.
evidence_signal: Across >2,000 runs, mean F1 increased from 0.46 to 0.72, precision from 56% to 90%, and mapping errors fell from 40.9% to 7.8% (all p < 0.001).
watch_item: Results came from synthetic notes and tool integration may vary by model, workflow, and EHR deployment constraints.
paper_title: Extraction of Human Phenotype Ontology (HPO) Concepts from Clinical Notes Utilizing Large Language Models (LLM) with Model Context Protocol (MCP)
